backend/modules/employee/routers/hr.py (1231 lines / 55921 bytes / 97 routes) is unreachable because the hr/ package shadows it - proven at runtime, not by inspection (importlib resolves to hr/__init__.py). This class of defect (a file and a same-named package coexisting in one directory, where the package silently wins) defeats every static file-placement law and every line-number citation a reviewer or agent makes against the shadowed file. I scanned every directory in backend/ for this pattern and found exactly ONE instance, so the blast radius is bounded - but the pattern recurs in the audit (CFM-005 cites hr.py line numbers that can never execute), and the same shadowing class is what makes domains/media invisible to rbac/catalog.py (missing __init__.py -> pkgutil.iter_modules skips it -> 4 declared feature atoms are unreachable and any future require_feature('media.*') would 403 for every role). Both are silent-by-construction defects that no CI gate currently detects.

16 files inside domains/ (12 promotions, 1 catalog, 1 orders, 1 suppliers) carry the header 'Retained for reference only; this file is NOT part of the running application.' That header is FALSE for 6 of them, and they are on the live request path: domains/promotions/services/admin_promotion_service.py is imported by modules/admin/routers/promotions.py:18 (an admin HTTP route) and domains/orders/ports.py:1600; four modules are star-imported by promotions/services/coupons/__init__.py:5-8; promotion_engine_service.py is named-imported by promotions/services/engine/__init__.py:12. Deleting on the strength of the comment would break production routes. It also spans 16 files in 4 domain packages plus a dangling reference to a domains/_parked directory that no longer exists - no single File:Line, and the whole risk is created by an untrustworthy self-description.
